zh: 这是胡雪岩第一次听见老张谈到他女儿，“叫”这个如何，“叫”那个如何，口气倒象是佣人听小姐的吩咐，不免有些诧异，但也明了阿珠在他家，真正是颗掌上明珠，她父母是无话不听的。“胡老爷，”老张又说，“我备了只小划子，划了你去。这里也实在太闹了，连我都厌烦，城河里清静得多。”于是下桥上船，向南穿过万安桥，折而往东，出了水关，就是极宽的护城河，一面城墙，一面菜畦，空阔无人。端午将近的黄梅天，蒸闷不堪，所以一到这地方，胡雪岩顿觉精神一爽，脱口赞了句：“阿珠倒真会挑地方！”“喏！”老张指着胡雪岩身后说：“我们的船停在那里。”船泊在一株柳树下面。那株杨柳极大，而且斜出临水，茂密的柳绿，覆盖了大半条船，不仔细看，还真不大容易发现。胡雪岩未到那条船上，已觉心旷神怡，把一脑子的海运局、钱庄之类的念头，忘了个干净。倒转身来，一直望着柳下的船。
en: This was the first time Hu had heard Old Zhang speak of his daughter. She had “told” one person to do this and another to do that; his tone suggested a servant carrying out his young mistress's instructions. Hu was a little surprised, but he also understood that A’zhu truly was the cherished jewel of the household. Her parents did whatever she asked. “Mr Hu,” Old Zhang continued, “I've brought a little skiff to row you over. It's much too noisy here. Even I find it tiresome. The moat is far quieter.” They went down from the bridge and boarded the skiff. Heading south beneath Wan'an Bridge, they turned east and passed through the water gate into the broad moat. On one side stood the city wall; on the other lay vegetable plots. The space was open and deserted. The Dragon Boat Festival was approaching, and the plum rains brought oppressive, steaming heat. As soon as they reached this place, Hu felt refreshed. “A’zhu certainly knows how to choose a spot!” he exclaimed. “There!” Old Zhang pointed behind him. “That's where our boat is.” It lay beneath an enormous willow leaning over the water, its dense green foliage sheltering more than half the vessel. Without looking carefully, one might easily have missed it. Even before reaching the boat, Hu felt his heart lift. Every thought of the Sea Transport Bureau and the bank vanished. He turned round and kept his eyes on the boat beneath the willow.

zh: 那条船上有也有在望，自然是阿珠。越行越近，看得越清楚，她穿一件浆洗得极挺拓的月白竹布衫，外面套一件玄色软缎的背心，一根漆黑的长辫子，仍然是她改不掉的习惯，把辫梢捞地手里捻弄着。小船划近，船上的伙计帮忙把他扶上大船，只见阿珠回和身向后梢喊道：“娘，好难请的贵客请到了！”阿珠的娘在后悄上做菜，分不开身来招呼，只高声带笑地说：“阿珠，你说话要摸摸良心，胡老爷一请就到，还说‘好难请’！”“也不知道哪个没有良心？”阿珠斜脱着胡雪岩，“人家的船是长途，我们的船就该是短程。”阿珠的娘深怕她女儿得罪了“贵客”，随即用呵斥的声音说道：“说话没轻没重，越说越不好了。”接着，放下锅铲，探身出来，一面在围裙上擦着双手，一面向胡雪岩含笑招呼：“胡老爷，你怎么这时候才来？阿珠一遍一遍在船头上望……”
en: Someone aboard was looking out too—A’zhu, naturally. As they approached, he could see her more clearly. She wore a pale blue cotton blouse, washed and starched until it was crisp, with a waistcoat of soft black satin. As always, she held the end of her long black braid and twisted it between her fingers, a habit she could never break. When the skiff drew alongside, the boat hand helped him aboard the larger vessel. A’zhu turned towards the stern and called, “Mother, our distinguished guest has arrived at last! Such trouble to persuade him!” Her mother was cooking at the stern and could not leave the stove to greet him. She merely called back with a laugh, “A’zhu, have a conscience! Mr Hu came the moment we asked him. How can you say he was hard to persuade?” “I wonder who has no conscience?” A’zhu glanced sideways at Hu. “Other people's boats get the long journeys. Ours is only good for short ones.” Afraid that her daughter would offend their distinguished guest, her mother immediately scolded her. “You don't know when to stop! Every word makes it worse.” Then she put down her spatula and leaned out, wiping her hands on her apron as she smiled at Hu. “Mr Hu, what kept you so long? A’zhu has been going to the bow to look for you over and over...”

zh: 这句话羞着了阿珠，原是白里泛红的一张脸，越发烧得如满天晚霞，抢着打断她的话说：“哪个一遍一遍在船头上望？瞎说八道！”说一完，只见长辫子一甩，扭身沿着船舷，往后舱就走。水上女儿走惯了的，看似风摆杨柳般摇摇欲坠，其实安然无事，但胡雪岩大为担心，慌忙喊道“阿珠，阿珠，你当心！不要掉到河里！”阿珠没有理他，不过听他那发急乱叫的声音，心里觉得很舒服，不由得就把脚步放慢了，一步一步很规矩地走着。“胡老爷，你看！”阿珠的娘仿佛万般无奈地，“疯疯癫癫，拿她真没法子。”“你也少罗嗦了！”老张这样埋怨他老婆，转脸又说，“胡老爷，你请舱里坐。”
en: This embarrassed A’zhu. Her fair cheeks, already tinged with pink, flamed like a sunset sky. She hastily interrupted. “Who's been going to the bow over and over? What nonsense!” With a flick of her long braid, she turned and walked along the gunwale towards the rear cabin. A girl brought up on the water was accustomed to this. She seemed to sway as precariously as a willow in the wind, but was perfectly safe. Hu, however, was alarmed. “A’zhu! A’zhu! Be careful! Don't fall into the river!” She ignored him, though his anxious cries pleased her. Almost without realising it, she slowed down and began taking careful, orderly steps. “Just look at her, Mr Hu!” her mother said with an air of complete helplessness. “Wild as a mad girl. There's nothing I can do with her.” “That's enough of your nagging too!” Old Zhang told his wife. Then he turned to Hu. “Please come and sit in the cabin.”

zh: 进舱就发现，这条船油漆一新，收拾得比以前更加整齐，便点点头说：“船修理过了？”“老早就要修了，一直凑不出一笔整数，多亏胡老爷上次照顾。”“以后机会还有。”胡雪岩说，“王大老爷放了湖州府，在杭州还有差使，常来常往，总有用得着你船的时候。”“那要请胡老爷替我们留意。”“本来，这种事不该我管。不过，你的船另当别论，我来想个办法。”胡雪岩沉吟着，想把老张的这条无锡快，当作海运局或者湖州府长期租用的“官船”，让他按月有一笔固定的收入。沉吟未定，阿珠又出现了，打来一盆脸水。这下提醒了老张，站起身说：“胡老爷先宽宽衣，洗洗脸，吃碗菜。哪天到临平，要吃些什么菜？等下叫阿珠的娘来跟胡老爷商量。”
en: Inside, Hu immediately noticed fresh paint and an even tidier appearance than before. He nodded. “You've had the boat repaired?” “It needed doing long ago. We could never put together enough money. We have your custom last time to thank.” “There will be more opportunities,” Hu said. “Mr Wang has been appointed to Huzhou, but he still has duties in Hangzhou. He'll often travel between the two. There are bound to be occasions when your boat is needed.” “Then we must ask you to keep us in mind.” “Ordinarily, arranging that sort of thing isn't my business. But your boat is a special case. I'll think of something.” He considered having the Sea Transport Bureau or the Huzhou prefecture hire Old Zhang's fast Wuxi boat on a long-term basis for official use, giving him a fixed monthly income. Before he had decided, A’zhu reappeared with a basin of water. This reminded Old Zhang of his duties as host. He stood. “First make yourself comfortable, Mr Hu, wash your face, and have some tea. What dishes would you like for the journey to Linping? I'll have A’zhu's mother come and discuss them with you presently.”

zh: 等老张一走，胡雪岩就轻松了，起身笑道，“阿珠，你的脾气必厉害！”“还要说人家！你自己不想想，一上了岸，把人家抛到九霄云外。平常不来还不要去说它，王大老爷到湖州上任，明明现成有船，他故意不用。你说说看，有没有这个道理？”她一面说一面替胡雪岩解钮扣卸去马褂、长衫，依偎在身边，又是那种无限幽怨的声音，胡雪岩自然是“别有一般滋味在心头。”等她低头去解他腋下的那颗钮扣上，他不由得就伸头去摸她的如退光黑漆般的头发，阿珠把头再往下低，避开了他的手，同时抗议：“不要动手动脚，把我头发都弄毛了！”
en: Once Old Zhang had gone, Hu relaxed. Rising with a smile, he said, “A’zhu, what a temper you have!” “And you still criticise me! Think of yourself. The moment you go ashore, you forget all about us. Never mind that you don't ordinarily visit. When Mr Wang goes to take up his appointment in Huzhou, there's a boat ready for him here, yet he deliberately won't use it. Tell me, is that reasonable?” As she spoke, she stood close beside Hu and helped unbutton and remove his outer jacket and long robe. Her voice was full of grievance, stirring feelings in him that he could scarcely name. When she lowered her head to undo a fastening beneath his arm, he reached out to touch her hair, black and glossy as polished lacquer. She ducked away from his hand and protested, “Keep your hands to yourself! You'll mess up my hair!”

zh: “你的头发是自己梳的？”“自然罗！我自己梳，我娘替我打辫子。我们这种人，难道还有丫头、老妈子来伺候的福气？”“也不见得没有。”胡雪岩说，“丫头、老妈子又何足为奇？”这话一说完，阿珠立刻抬起眼来，双目流转，在他的脸上绕了一下，马上又低下头去，捞起他的长衫下摆，解掉最后一个扣子，卸去外衣，然后绞一把手巾送到他手里。他发现她眼中有期待的神色，不用说，那是希望他对她刚才所说的那句话，有个进一步的解释。但是他已悔出言轻率，便装做不解，很快地扯到别的事。
en: “Do you comb it yourself?” “Naturally! I comb it, and Mother plaits it. Do you suppose people like us are fortunate enough to have maids and serving women to wait on us?” “You might be,” Hu said. “There's nothing so extraordinary about having servants.” At once she raised her eyes and searched his face, then looked down again. Gathering the skirt of his robe, she undid the last fastening, removed the outer garment, and wrung out a towel for him. He saw expectation in her eyes. Clearly she hoped he would explain what he had just said. But he already regretted his rash words, so he pretended not to understand and quickly turned to something else.

zh: 这件事，足以让阿珠立刻忘掉他刚才的那句话，他解开他带来的那个包袱，里面是一个小小的箱子，仿照保险箱的做法。用铁皮所装，漆成墨绿色，也装有暗锁。“这是什么箱子？”“ ‘杜十娘怒沉百宝箱’的百宝箱。”他把暗锁打开，相内却只有“四宝”，一瓶香水，一个八音盒，一把日本女人插在头上当装饰的象牙细篦，一只景泰蓝嵌珠的女表。
en: The new subject was enough to make A’zhu forget his remark immediately. He unwrapped the bundle he had brought. Inside was a small chest made in imitation of a safe, clad in sheet iron, painted dark green, and fitted with a concealed lock. “What sort of chest is that?” “A treasure chest, like the one in the story of Du Shiniang, who sank her treasure chest in anger.” He opened the lock. This chest, however, contained only four treasures: a bottle of perfume, a musical box, a fine ivory comb of the kind Japanese women wore as an ornament, and a lady's watch in pearl-set cloisonné enamel.

zh: 阿珠惊多于喜，看看这样，摸摸那样，好半天说不出话。胡雪岩先把牙篦插在她头发上，接着把那只表用钥匙上足了弦，以自己的金表校准了时刻，替阿珠挂在钮扣上，再把八音盒子开足了发条，让它叮叮当当响着，最后拿起那瓶香水，阿珠忽然失声喊道：“不要，不要！”胡雪岩愕然：“不要什么？”“傻瓜！”阿珠嫣然一笑，“不要打开来！”这时老张和那船伙计，为从未听过的叮叮当当的声音所招引，都在船舱外探望，要弄明白是什么东西在响？阿珠却不容他们看个究竟，一手八音盒，一手香水，头插牙蓖，衣襟上晃荡着那只表，急忙忙走向后梢，到她娘那里“献宝”去了。
en: A’zhu was more astonished than delighted. She looked at one thing and touched another, unable to speak for a long while. Hu first placed the ivory comb in her hair. Then he wound the watch with its key, set it by his own gold watch, and hung it from one of her buttons. Next he wound the musical box and let its tinkling notes ring out. Finally he picked up the perfume. A’zhu suddenly cried, “No, no!” He looked surprised. “No what?” “Silly!” She smiled. “Don't open it!” Drawn by the unfamiliar chiming, Old Zhang and the boat hand peered into the cabin, trying to discover what was making the sound. A’zhu gave them no chance to inspect it. With the musical box in one hand and the perfume in the other, the ivory comb in her hair and the watch swinging from her clothes, she hurried to the stern to show her mother her treasures.

zh: 于是只听得她们母女俩赞叹说笑的声音，最后是做娘的在告诫：“好好去放好。有人的地方少拿出来，胡家的阿毛手脚不干净，当心她顺手牵羊。““怕什么！我锁在‘百宝箱’里！”“什么‘百宝箱’？”“喏，”大概是阿珠在比划，“这么长，这么宽，是铁的，还有暗锁，怎么开法只有我一个人晓得，偷不走的。”原来是首饰箱！“阿珠的娘说：”傻丫头，人家不会连箱子一起偷？““啊！”阿珠醒悟了。接着便又重新出现在中舱，高兴之外，似乎还有些忧虑的神色。
en: Hu heard mother and daughter exclaiming, laughing, and talking. At last the mother cautioned her: “Put them away safely. Don't keep bringing them out when other people are about. A'mao, the Hu girl, has light fingers. Mind she doesn't help herself.” “What is there to fear? I'll lock them in my treasure chest!” “What treasure chest?” “Look,” A’zhu said, presumably indicating its size with her hands. “It's this long and this wide, made of iron, with a hidden lock. I'm the only one who knows how to open it. No one can steal them.” “Oh, a jewellery box!” her mother said. “Silly girl, couldn't someone steal the box as well?” “Ah!” That had not occurred to A’zhu. She soon reappeared in the middle cabin, still delighted, but now looking a little anxious too.

zh: 为了知道她的忧虑想安慰她，胡雪岩招把手说：“阿珠，你过来，我有话说。”“你说好了！”她这样回答，一面打开那只百宝箱，除了头上的那把蓖以外，其余“三宝”都收入箱内。却把个开了盖的箱子捧在手里，凝视不休。“你到底想不想听我的话。”“好，好！我听。”阿珠急忙答应，锁好箱子，走到胡雪岩对面坐下，右手支颐，偏着头等他开口。这又是一个极动人的姿态，胡雪岩也偏着头紧盯着她看。阿珠大概心里还在百宝箱里，以致视而不见。
en: Understanding her anxiety and wanting to reassure her, Hu beckoned. “A’zhu, come here. I have something to tell you.” “Go ahead!” she answered. Opening the chest, she put away the three treasures, leaving only the comb in her hair. Yet she continued to hold the open box and gaze into it. “Do you want to listen to me or not?” “Yes, yes! I'm listening.” She hurriedly locked it and sat opposite him, her chin supported by her right hand and her head tilted as she waited for him to speak. He found the pose so appealing that he too tilted his head and gazed at her. A’zhu's thoughts were apparently still in the treasure chest: she looked at him without seeing him.

zh: 她不作声，他也不开口，好久，她方省悟，张皇而抱歉地问道：“你，你刚才说什么？”“咦！”胡雪岩故意装作十分诧异地，“我说了半天，你一句都没有听进去？”阿珠为他一诈，歉意越发浓了，陪着笑说：“对不起！我想起一桩要紧事情。”“什么要紧事？”原是托词，让他钉紧了一问。得要想几句话来圆自己的谎，偏偏脑筋越紧越笨，越笨越急，涨红了脸，好半天说不出一句话来。“好了，好了！”胡雪岩大为不忍，“不便说就不说。”“是啊，这桩事情不便说。”阿珠如释重负似地笑道：“现在，你有什么话，请你尽管话，我一定留心听。”
en: She said nothing, and neither did he. Eventually she came to herself and asked in apologetic confusion, “What—what were you saying?” “Why!” Hu pretended to be astonished. “I've been talking all this time, and you haven't heard a word?” Taken in, she became even more apologetic. “I'm sorry,” she said with a conciliatory smile. “I suddenly remembered something important.” “What was it?” It had merely been an excuse. Now that he pressed her, she had to find something to make her story convincing. The more she strained to think, the less she could manage; the less she could manage, the more anxious she grew. Her face reddened, and for a long time she could not produce a word. “Never mind, never mind!” Hu could not bear to torment her. “If it's private, don't tell me.” “Yes, it's something private.” Relieved, she smiled. “Now say whatever you wanted to say. I'll listen carefully.”

zh: “我劝你，不要把你娘的话太当真！”他放低了声音说，“身外之物要看得开些……”他讲了一套“身外之物”的道理，人以役物，不可为物所役，心受之物固然要当心被窃，但为了怕被窃，不敢拿出来用，甚至时进忧虑，处处分心，这就是为物所役，倒不如无此一物。“所以，”他说，“你的脑筋一定要转过来。丢掉就丢掉，没有什么了不得！不然，我送你这几样东西，倒变成害了你了。”他把这番道理说得很透彻，无奈阿珠大不以为然，“你倒说得大方，‘丢掉就丢掉’！你不心疼我心疼。”她忽有怨怼，“你这个人就是这样，说丢掉就丢掉，一点情分都没有。对人对东西都一样！”“你说‘对人对东西部一样’，这个‘人’是哪个？”“你还问得出口？”阿珠冷笑，“可见得你心里早没有那个‘人’了！”
en: “My advice is not to take your mother's warning too seriously,” he said, lowering his voice. “Don't let possessions weigh on your mind...” He explained his view of material things. People should make use of possessions, not become their servants. Naturally one should guard a treasured object against theft. But if fear of losing it prevented one from using it, or caused constant anxiety and distraction, one had become its servant. Better not to own it at all. “So,” he concluded, “you must change the way you think. If something is lost, it's lost. It isn't the end of the world! Otherwise my presents will have done you harm instead of good.” He had made his reasoning perfectly clear, but A’zhu strongly disagreed. “How generous you sound! ‘If it's lost, it's lost!’ You may not mind, but I do.” Suddenly her tone grew resentful. “That's just like you. You can throw something away without a second thought. You have no feeling at all—for people or possessions!” “You say ‘people or possessions.’ Which person do you mean?” “You can actually ask?” She gave a bitter little laugh. “That proves you've long since forgotten that person!”

zh: “亏你怎么想出来了？”胡雪岩有些懊恼，“我们在讲那几样东西，你无缘无故会扯到人上面？我劝你不必太看重身外之物，正是为了看重你，你连这点道理都想不明白？再说，我那么忙，你娘来一叫我就来，还要怎么样呢？至于王大老爷上任要雇船，你也得替我想想，照我在王大老爷面前的身分，好不好去管这种小事情？““我晓得，都归庶务老爷管，不过你提一声也不要紧啊！”“这不就是插手去管吗？你总晓得，这都有回扣的，我一管，庶务就不敢拿回扣了。别人不知道用你家的船，另有道理，只说我想要回扣。我怎么能背这种名声？”阿珠听了这一番话，很快地看了他一眼，把眼皮垂下去，长长的睫毛闪动着，好久不作声。
en: “How did you manage to think of that?” Hu was a little exasperated. “We were talking about those presents. Why suddenly drag people into it? I tell you not to care too much about possessions precisely because I care about you. Can't you understand even that? Besides, busy as I am, I came the moment your mother invited me. What more do you want? As for hiring a boat for Mr Wang's departure, put yourself in my position. Given my standing with him, would it be proper for me to interfere in such a small matter?” “I know. The general affairs officer arranges all that. But what harm would there be in mentioning it?” “Wouldn't that be interfering? Surely you know there are commissions on these things. Once I intervened, the officer wouldn't dare take his commission. Other people wouldn't know I had a different reason for choosing your boat. They'd say I wanted the commission myself. How could I let people think that of me?” A’zhu gave him a quick glance, then lowered her eyes. Her long lashes fluttered, and she remained silent for some time.

zh: 那是石火电光般的一瞥，但包含着自悔、致歉、佩服、感激，以及求取谅解的许多意思在内，好象在说：你不说明白，我哪里知道？多因为我的见识不如你，想不到其中有这么多道理。我只当你有意不用我家的船，是特意要避开我，其实你是爱莫能助。一请就来，你也不是有意避我。看来是我错怪了人！也难为你，一直逼到最后你才说破！我不对，你也不对，你应该晓得我心里着急，何不一来先就解释这件事？倘或你早说明白，我怎么说那许多叫人刺心的话，也许你倒不在乎，但是你可知道我说这些话心里是如何懊悔？
en: The glance was brief as a flash of lightning, yet it contained regret, apology, admiration, gratitude, and a plea for understanding. It seemed to say: How could I know unless you explained? I don't know as much as you do. I never imagined there were so many things to consider. I thought you deliberately refused our boat because you wanted to avoid me, when really you wanted to help but couldn't. You came as soon as we asked, so you weren't avoiding me either. It seems I misjudged you! And you had to be pushed to the very last before you would explain. I was wrong, but so were you. You should have known how anxious I was. Why didn't you explain when you first arrived? If you'd told me sooner, would I have said all those hurtful things? Perhaps you don't mind, but do you know how bitterly I regret saying them?

zh: 女儿家的曲曲心事，胡雪岩再机警也难猜透，不过她有愧歉之意，却是看得出来的。他的性情是最不愿意做煞风景的事，所以自己先就一下撇开，摇着手说：“好了；好了，话说过就算数了，不要去东想西想。喂，我问你。”最后一句声音大了些，仿佛突如其来似地，阿珠微吃一惊，抬起头来睁大了双眼看着他。“你娘今天弄了些什么菜给我吃？”“我还不晓得。”“咦！”胡雪岩说，“这就怪了，你怎么会不晓得。莫非……”他本来想取笑她，说是“莫非一遍一遍在船头上望？”话到口旁，警觉到这个玩笑开不得，所以缩住了口。话是没有说出口，脸上那诡秘的笑容却依然在。阿珠也是极精灵的人，顿时就逼着问：“莫非什么？”“莫非，”胡雪岩随口答道：“你在生我的气，所以懒得去问？”“你说这话没有良心！”她说，但也并不见得生气，却转身走了出去。
en: However quick-witted Hu might be, he could scarcely unravel all the twists of a young woman's heart. He could see, though, that she felt sorry. He hated spoiling a pleasant occasion, so he dismissed the whole matter with a wave. “There, there. We've said our piece. Don't go worrying about it. Now, tell me something.” His last words were a little louder and seemed so sudden that A’zhu started and looked up with wide eyes. “What has your mother cooked for me today?” “I don't know yet.” “Really? That's odd. How can you not know? Unless...” He had been about to tease her: unless she had spent all her time at the bow, looking out for him. Just as the words reached his lips, he realised that this joke would be unwise and stopped. Though he had said nothing, his mischievous smile remained. A’zhu was sharp too. “Unless what?” she demanded at once. “Unless,” he improvised, “you were angry with me and couldn't be bothered to ask.” “You have no conscience, saying that!” Yet she did not seem angry. She simply turned and went out.

zh: 很快地，她又走了回来，手里多了一个托盘，里面一只盖碗，揭开碗盖来看，是冰糖煮的新鲜莲子、湖菱和芡实，正是最时新、最珍贵的点心。另外有两只小碟子，一黄一红，黄的是桂花酱，红的是玫瑰卤，不但香味浓郁，而且鲜艳夺目。“一天就替你弄这一碗点心，你还说我懒得管你，是不是没有良心？”胡雪岩看碗中的莲子等物，剥得极其干净，粒粒完整，这才知道她花的功夫惊人，心里倒觉得老大不过意。“吃啊！”阿珠说，“两样卤子随你自己调，我看玫瑰卤子好。”“我实在舍不得吃，留着闻闻看看。”“咄！”阿珠笑了，“跟伢儿一样。”说着用小银匙挑了一匙玫瑰卤调在碗里，然后往他面前一推，“冷了不好吃了。”
en: She soon returned with a tray bearing a covered bowl. When she lifted the lid, he saw fresh lotus seeds, lake-grown water caltrops, and gorgon seeds simmered in rock sugar: the choicest and most prized delicacies of the season. Two small dishes accompanied them, one yellow with osmanthus preserve, the other red with rose syrup, vividly coloured as well as richly fragrant. “I've spent all day preparing this one bowl for you. Yet you say I can't be bothered with you! Isn't that heartless?” Hu saw how carefully everything had been peeled, each seed perfectly whole. Only then did he realise the astonishing amount of work she had put in, and he felt deeply apologetic. “Eat!” she said. “Add whichever flavouring you like. I think the rose syrup is better.” “I can hardly bear to eat it. I'd like to keep it here to look at and smell.” “Oh!” A’zhu laughed. “You're just like a child.” With a little silver spoon, she stirred a spoonful of rose syrup into the bowl and pushed it towards him. “It won't taste as good when it's cold.”

zh: “你自己呢？”“我啊！找自己才懒得弄呢。倒是我爹叨你的光，难得吃这么一碗细巧点心。”“真正是细巧点心！皇帝在宫里，也不过如此。对不！”胡雪岩又说，“宫里虽然四时八节，有各地进贡的时鲜货，到底路远迢迢，哪里一上市就有得吃？”阿珠听了他的话，十分高兴，“这样说起来，你的福气比皇帝还要好？”她拿手指刮着脸羞他：“说大话不要本钱，世界上再没有比你脸皮厚的人！”说完，自己倒又笑了，接着扭身往后，到后梢去帮忙开饭。
en: “What about yours?” “Mine? I couldn't be bothered to make it for myself. But Father has benefited from your visit. He rarely gets such a delicate treat.” “A delicate treat indeed! The emperor in his palace could have nothing finer. No, wait,” Hu added. “Throughout the year, at every festival, the palace receives seasonal delicacies as tribute from everywhere. But they have so far to travel. How could he enjoy them the moment they first appear?” A’zhu was delighted. “Then are you saying you're luckier than the emperor?” She drew a finger down her cheek to shame him. “Boasting costs nothing! No one in the world has a thicker skin than you.” Then she laughed herself, turned, and went to the stern to help serve the meal.

zh: 胡雪岩倒不是说大活，真的自觉有南面王不易之乐，一人坐在爽气扑人的船窗边，吃着那碗点心，眼望着平畴绿野，心境是说不出的那种开阔轻松。当然，阿珠仿佛仍旧在他眼前，只要想到便看得见，听得到，一颦一笑，无不可人。他开始认真考虑他与她之间的将来了。
en: Hu was not merely boasting. He truly felt a happiness he would not exchange for an emperor's throne. Sitting alone beside the cabin window, with fresh air flowing in, he ate his sweet dish and looked across the level fields and green countryside, his mind light and spacious beyond description. A’zhu, of course, still seemed to be before his eyes. Whenever he thought of her, he could see her and hear her; every frown and smile pleased him. He began seriously to consider their future together.

zh: 想不多久，思路便被打断，阿珠来开饭了，抹桌子，摆碗筷，一面告诉他说：“四菜一汤，两个碟子，够你吃的了。今天有黄花鱼，有莼菜。”话没有说完，阿珠的娘已端了菜来，密炙文火，新鲜荷叶粉蒸肉，卤备瓜蒸黄花鱼，炸响铃，另外两个下酒的冷碟，虾米拌黄瓜，卤什件。然后自己替胡雪岩斟了杯“竹叶青”，嘴里说着客气话。“多谢，多谢！”胡雪岩指着桌面说：“这么许多菜，我无论如何吃不下。大家一起来！”“从没有这个规矩！”阿珠的娘也知道他的弦外之意，所以接着又自己把话拉回来，“不过一个人吃闷酒也无趣，让阿珠敬胡老爷一杯。”阿珠是巴不得她娘有这一句，立刻掉转身子，去拿了一小酒杯，同时把她的那双银筷子也捏了在手里。
en: Before long, his thoughts were interrupted. A’zhu came to lay the meal, wiping the table and setting out bowls and chopsticks. “Four dishes and a soup, with two little plates as well. That should be enough for you. We've yellow croaker today, and water shield.” Before she had finished, her mother arrived with the food: a roast cooked over gentle heat, pork coated in rice meal and steamed in fresh lotus leaves, yellow croaker steamed with pickled melon, and crisp bean-curd rolls. There were also two cold dishes to go with the wine, cucumber with dried shrimps and assorted braised meats. Her mother poured Hu a cup of Zhuyeqing wine, accompanying it with courteous words. “Thank you, thank you!” He gestured at the table. “I couldn't possibly eat all this. Everyone come and join me!” “That would be quite against the rules!” But A’zhu's mother understood his unspoken meaning, and immediately softened her refusal. “Still, drinking alone is no pleasure. Let A’zhu offer you a cup.” This was precisely what A’zhu had hoped to hear. She turned at once to fetch a small wine cup, bringing her silver chopsticks too.

zh: “胡老爷，到底哪天要用船？”“五月切七一早动身。”他说，“来去总得两天。”“宁愿打宽些。”阿珠在旁接口，“两天不够的。”“也对。”胡雪岩说，“这样，加一倍算四天好了。”“菜呢？”“随你配，随你配！”胡雪岩是准备好了，从小褂口袋里取出一张银票，递了过去，“你先收了，不够我再补。”阿珠的娘是识得字的，看那银票是二十两，连忙答道：“有得多！哪里用得着这许多？”“端午要到了。多了你自己买点东西吃，节礼我就‘折干’了。”阿珠的娘想了想说：“好，多的银子就算存在我这里。好在胡老爷以后总还有坐我们船的时候。”说完，她就退了出去。
en: “Mr Hu, exactly when will you need the boat?” “We leave early on the seventh of the fifth month,” he replied. “The journey there and back will take at least two days.” “Better allow plenty of time,” A’zhu put in. “Two days won't be enough.” “Quite right. Let's double it and say four.” “And the food?” “Choose whatever you like!” Hu had come prepared. He took a banknote from the pocket of his short jacket and handed it over. “Take this for now. If it isn't enough, I'll make up the difference.” A’zhu's mother could read. Seeing that it was for twenty taels, she hastily answered, “It's more than enough! We couldn't possibly need so much.” “The Dragon Boat Festival is nearly here. Buy yourselves something to eat with what's left. Consider it my festival present in cash.” She thought a moment. “Very well. I'll keep the balance on account for you. You're sure to use our boat again.” With that, she withdrew.

zh: 胡雪岩顾不得说话！一半也是有意如此，不喝酒先吃菜，百实在也是真正的享用，连着吃了好几筷鱼，才抬头笑道：“阿珠，我有个办法，最好有这样一位丈母娘，那我的口福就好了！”表面上是笑话，暗地里是试探，遇着情分还不够的女孩子，这就是唐突，会惹得对方生气，非挨骂不可。但在阿珠听来，又不以为是试探，竟是他吐露真意，作了承诺，顿时脸也红了，心也跳了，忸怩万分，恨不得就从窗口，“扑通”一声跳到河里去泅水，躲开他那双眼睛。幸好，胡雪岩只说话时看了她一眼，说完依旧埋头大嚼。不过阿珠眼前的羞窘虽无人得见，心里的波澜却连自己都觉得难以应付，她霍地一下站起来就跑。这不暇考虑的一个动作，等做出来了，心里却又不安，怕他误会她生了气，所以顺口说了句：“我去看看，汤好了没有？”
en: Hu was too busy eating to talk, partly by design. Before touching his wine he set about the food, which he really did relish. After several mouthfuls of fish, he looked up with a smile. “A’zhu, I've had an idea. If only I had a mother-in-law like this, I should eat wonderfully well!” On the surface it was a joke; beneath it, a test. With a girl who was not sufficiently attached to him, such a remark would have been presumptuous and bound to provoke an angry rebuke. But A’zhu did not hear it as a test. To her he had revealed his true feelings and made a promise. Her cheeks reddened, her heart pounded, and she felt so shy that she longed to jump through the window into the river and swim away from his gaze. Fortunately he had glanced at her only while speaking, then bent over his food again. No one saw her embarrassment, but even she scarcely knew how to manage the turmoil inside her. Suddenly she sprang up and ran. Having acted without thinking, she then worried that he might suppose she was angry. “I'll go and see whether the soup is ready,” she said quickly.

zh: 原是句托词。一脸的红晕，她也羞于见娘，回到自己的铺上，抚着胸，摸着脸，只是对自己说：把心定下来！心一定又想起她爹娘那天晚上的话，老夫妇没有防到隔舱有耳，说来一无顾忌，“女大不中留，我看阿珠茶不思，饭不想，好象有点……”她爹没有再说下去。“有点什么？”“好象害相思病。”“死鬼！”她娘骂他，“自己女儿，说得这样难听！”“我是实话。你说，我是不是老实话？”她娘不响，好半天才问：“你看，那位胡老爷人怎么样？”“这个人将来一定要发达的……”“我不是说他发达不发达。”她娘抢着又说，“我是说，你看他有没有良心？”
en: It was only an excuse. With her cheeks so flushed, she was ashamed to face her mother as well. She returned to her own berth, pressed a hand over her pounding heart, touched her face, and kept telling herself to calm down. As she grew calmer, she remembered a conversation between her parents one night. Unaware that she could hear them through the cabin partition, they had spoken freely. “You can't keep a grown daughter at home,” her father had said. “A’zhu has no appetite for food or tea. She seems a little...” He stopped. “A little what?” “As if she's lovesick.” “You wretch!” her mother scolded. “How can you speak so disrespectfully of your own daughter?” “I'm only telling the truth. Am I not?” Her mother said nothing. After a long silence she asked, “What do you think of this Mr Hu?” “He's certain to get on in the world...” “I'm not asking whether he'll get on.” She interrupted. “I'm asking whether you think he has a conscience.”

zh: “你怕他对阿珠没有良心？我看，这倒不会。不过，你说的，不肯阿珠给人家做小。何以现在又问这话？”“我不肯又怎么样？阿珠喜欢他，有什么办法？”“怎么样呢？我只看她茶不思，饭不想，从来没有在我面前提过胡老爷。”“在你面前当然不会。”阿珠的娘说，“在我面前，不晓得提过多少回了，无缘无故就会扯到姓胡的头上，这一趟到上海的客人，不是很刮皮吗？阿珠背后说起来，总是‘人家胡老爷不象他’，‘人家胡老爷才是好客人’，你听听！“
en: “You're afraid he wouldn't treat A’zhu properly? I don't think that would happen. But you said you wouldn't let her become anyone's concubine. Why ask this now?” “What difference does my refusing make? A’zhu likes him. What can we do?” “How do you know? I've only noticed that she won't eat or drink. She's never mentioned Mr Hu to me.” “Of course she wouldn't mention him to you,” her mother said. “But she's spoken of him to me more times than I could count. Whatever we're discussing, she finds a way of bringing him in. That passenger we took to Shanghai this time was terribly stingy, wasn't he? When A’zhu spoke of him afterwards, it was always ‘Mr Hu isn't like him’ or ‘Mr Hu is what I call a good passenger.’ There, what do you make of that?”

zh: “那么，你现在到底是怎么个意思呢？”“我也想穿了，只要小两口感情好，做大做小也就不管它了！不过，”她娘换了种敬重丈夫的语气：“这总要做老子的作主。”“也由不得我作主。我老早说过，照我的意思，最好挑个老实的，一夫一妻，苦就苦一点。只是你不肯，她不愿。那就你们娘儿俩自己去商量好了。”“女儿不是我一个人的，你不要推出不管。”阿珠的娘说，“你也去打听打听，到底胡老爷住在哪里？信和的张老板一定晓得，你去问他！”“问到了做什么？你要去看他？”“一则看他，二则看他太太，如果是只雌老虎，那就叫阿珠死了这条心吧！”
en: “Then what exactly do you think now?” “I've come to see it this way: provided the two of them care for one another, I won't worry about her being wife or concubine. Still...” Her tone became respectful towards her husband. “Her father must decide.” “It's hardly for me to decide either. I told you long ago what I'd prefer: an honest fellow, with just the one wife. If life were a little harder, so be it. But you wouldn't agree, and neither would she. Then let the two of you settle it between yourselves.” “She's not my daughter alone. Don't push it all away and wash your hands of it,” her mother said. “Go and find out where Mr Hu lives. Manager Zhang at Xinhe must know. Ask him!” “And once I know? Do you mean to visit him?” “First to see him, and then to see his wife. If she's a tigress, A’zhu must put him out of her mind.”

zh: 这是十天前的话，果然寻着了“胡老爷”，而且一请就来。就不知道她娘看见了胡太太没有，为人如何？阿珠心里这样在转着念头。唉！她自己对自己不满，这样容易明白的事，何以好久都猜不透？只要到了胡家，自然见着了胡太太，如果胡太太真个是只“雌老虎”，从娘那里先就死了心，决不肯承揽这笔短途的生意，更不会待他这样子的殷勤亲热。照此看来，娘不但见着了胡太太，而且看得胡太太十分贤惠，有气量，将来女儿嫁过去，有把握不会吃亏受气，所以今天完全是象“毛脚女婿”上门一般待他。这不是明摆着的事，为何自己思前想后一直想不通？这下倒是想通了，但刚有些定下来的心，却越发乱了。
en: That had been ten days ago. They had indeed found Mr Hu, and he had come as soon as he was invited. But had her mother seen Mrs Hu? What sort of person was she? A’zhu turned these questions over in her mind. How foolish she was! Why had she taken so long to understand something so obvious? If her mother had gone to the Hu house, she must have met Mrs Hu. Had the wife really been a tigress, Mother would have abandoned the idea herself. She would never have agreed to this short voyage, still less have treated him with such warmth and attention. Clearly, then, Mother had not only met Mrs Hu but found her kind and generous enough to be sure that her daughter would suffer no ill treatment if she married into the household. That was why she had welcomed him today exactly as she would a prospective son-in-law making his first visit. Wasn't it plain? Why had she thought round and round without seeing it? Now she understood, but her heart, only just beginning to settle, grew more agitated than ever.

zh: “阿珠啊！”她听得她娘在喊，“来把汤端了去！”这一叫使得阿珠大窘，自己摸一摸脸，简直烫手，料想脸色一定红得象岸上的榴花一样，但不答应也不得，便高声先答一句：“来了！”“快来啊！汤要冷了。”万般无奈，只好这样答道：“娘，你自己端一端，我手上不空。”“你在做啥？”什么也不做，只象一碗热汤一样，摆在那里，等自己的脸冷下来。她又用凉水洗了一把脸，脱去软缎背心，刚解衣钮，听得一声门响，吓一大跳，赶紧双手抱胸，掩住衣襟。“走进来也不说一声！”她埋怨她娘，“吓得我魂灵都出窍了。”“你也是，这时候擦什么身？”她娘催她：“快点！你也来帮着招呼招呼。”这一下妙极，“手上不空”的原因也有了，脸上的颜色也遮掩了。阿珠大为得意，把手巾一丢，扣好衣钮，拿下摆抹一抹平，重新走到了前舱。
en: “A’zhu!” she heard her mother call. “Come and take the soup in!” The call embarrassed her terribly. She touched her face: it was almost hot enough to burn her hand. Surely she must be as red as the pomegranate blossoms on shore. Yet she had to answer. “Coming!” she called first. “Hurry! The soup will get cold.” Desperate, she replied, “Mother, take it yourself. My hands are full.” “What are you doing?” Nothing at all. Like a bowl of hot soup, she was simply waiting there to cool. She washed her face again in cold water, removed her satin waistcoat, and had just begun undoing her blouse when the door opened. Startled, she quickly held the garment closed. “You might say something before coming in!” she complained to her mother. “You frightened the life out of me.” “And why choose this moment to wash?” her mother urged. “Hurry up and help entertain our guest.” How fortunate! Now she had both an explanation for being occupied and an excuse for her flushed face. Very pleased with herself, A’zhu dropped the towel, fastened her blouse, smoothed its hem, and returned to the forward cabin.

zh: 胡雪岩已经在吃饭了，一碗刚刚吃完，她伸手去接饭碗，他摇摇头说：“吃得太饱了！”“那么你多吃点汤。这碗三丝莼菜汤，是我娘的拿手菜。”“没有一样不拿手，请王大老爷那天，大致就照这个样子，再添两个炒菜，弄只汽锅鸡。”“什么叫汽锅鸡？”阿珠笑道：“江西人补碗，‘叽咕叽’！”胡雪岩忍不住笑了，笑停了说：“原来你也有不晓得的菜！汽锅鸡是云南菜，王大老爷是福建人，生长在云南，所以喜欢云南口味。汽锅鸡我也是在他家头一回吃，做法我也学会了，等下我再传授给你娘。”“不要，不要，你教我好了。”阿珠往后看了看，“ 不要给我娘晓得。”“咦！这为啥？”“我娘总说我笨手笨脚，没有一样菜烧得入味的。我现在也要学一样她不会的，只怕见都没有见过，那就尽由得我说了。”
en: Hu had begun his rice and had just finished a bowl. When she reached to take it for a refill, he shook his head. “I've eaten far too much!” “Then have some more soup. Water-shield soup with three shredded ingredients is Mother's speciality.” “Everything is her speciality. When we entertain Mr Wang, serve much the same, with two extra stir-fried dishes and a steam-pot chicken.” “What's steam-pot chicken?” A’zhu laughed. “Qi-gu-ji! It sounds like the cry of those Jiangxi men who mend bowls!” Hu could not help laughing. When he recovered, he said, “So there is a dish you don't know! Steam-pot chicken comes from Yunnan. Mr Wang's family is from Fujian, but he grew up in Yunnan, so he likes Yunnan flavours. I first ate it at his house and learnt how to make it. I'll teach your mother later.” “No, no. Teach me.” A’zhu glanced towards the rear. “Don't let Mother know.” “Why ever not?” “Mother's always saying I'm clumsy and can't cook a single dish properly. I want to learn something she can't make—perhaps something she's never even seen. Then whatever I say about it will have to be right.”

zh: “好，我教你！”胡雪岩把汽锅鸡的做法传授了她。“这并不难嘛！”“本来就不难，只是那只锅不容易找，我送你们一个。”胡雪岩又说：“我倒要尝一尝你这个徒弟的手艺，看比我另外的一个徒弟是好是坏？”“另外一个徒弟是哪个？”胡雪岩笑笔不响。阿珠也猜到了是谁，心里顿起一种异样的感觉，好象有些不舒服，但又不能不关心。她又想，不问下去倒显得自己有什么忌讳似地，十分不妥。于是问道：“是胡太太？”“当然是她。”“胡太太的这样菜，一定做得道地？”“也不见得。”胡雪岩说，“她不大会做菜，也不大喜欢下厨房。”“那么喜欢什么呢？”
en: “Very well, I'll teach you!” Hu explained how to make steam-pot chicken. “That's not difficult!” “It isn't. Only the special pot is hard to find. I'll give you one.” He added, “I must taste my new pupil's cooking and see whether it's better or worse than my other pupil's.” “Who is your other pupil?” Hu smiled without answering. A’zhu guessed, and a strange feeling rose in her, vaguely uncomfortable but impossible to ignore. Then she thought that refusing to ask would make her seem afraid of the subject, which would be very wrong. “Mrs Hu?” “Of course.” “Then she must make this dish just as it should be made?” “Not necessarily,” he said. “She isn't much of a cook and doesn't particularly like the kitchen.” “What does she like, then?”

zh: 胡雪岩有些猜到，她是在打听他太太的性情，因而想到她娘那天也可能借送食物为名，特意来观望风色。如果自己的猜想不错，只怕今天就要有个了断。这是个难题，在自己这方面来说，对于阿珠的态度，根本还未到可以作最后决定的时候，那就得想个什么好办法来搪塞，既要达到自己的目的，又要不伤阿珠的感情。
en: Hu began to suspect that A’zhu was sounding him out about his wife's character. Perhaps her mother, too, had used the delivery of food as an excuse to visit and assess the situation. If he was right, they might expect some definite settlement today. This was difficult. He himself was nowhere near ready to make a final decision about A’zhu. He must find a tactful way of putting them off that would achieve his purpose without hurting her feelings.

zh: “咦！怎么了，忽然变哑巴了？”阿珠见他久久不语，这样催问。“我忽然想起一桩要紧事。”胡雪岩顺口掩饰着，“刚才谈到什么地方了？”阿珠倒又不关心他太太的爱好了，咬着嘴唇，微垂着眼，死瞪住他看。“我要说你了，”胡雪岩笑道，“莫非你也变了哑巴？”“我也忽然想起一桩事，我要看你刚才说的话是真，是假？”“你以为我说有要紧事是骗你？”“不是什么骗我，你在打主意要走了！”“你的心思真多。不过，”胡雪岩望着窗外，“天快黑了，这地方上岸不便，而且看样子要下雨。我说句实话，你不说我倒记不起，你一说正好提醒我，我该走了。”
en: “What's wrong? Have you suddenly lost your voice?” A’zhu asked when he remained silent. “I've just remembered something important,” he said to cover his thoughts. “What were we talking about?” A’zhu was no longer interested in his wife's preferences. Biting her lip, she lowered her eyes a little and stared fixedly at him. “Now it's my turn to ask,” Hu said with a smile. “Have you lost your voice too?” “I've suddenly thought of something as well. I want to see whether what you just said was true.” “Do you think I invented that important matter?” “It isn't a question of inventing it. You're trying to think how to leave!” “You do imagine things. Still...” Hu looked out of the window. “It's getting dark, landing here isn't easy, and it looks like rain. To tell you the truth, it hadn't occurred to me until you mentioned it. You've reminded me: I ought to go.”

zh: 阿珠心里十分生气，明明早就想走了，还要说便宜话，于是转身向外，故意拉长了声音喊船伙计：“阿四，搭跳板，送客！”“还早啊！”她娘马上应声，“胡老爷再坐一歇。”“不要留他！天黑了，要下雨了，路上不好走，等下滑一跤，都怪你！”明明负气，偏是呖呖莺声，入耳只觉好听有趣。胡雪岩无论如何忍不下心来说要走，笑笑答道：“我不走，是阿珠在赶我。”“阿珠又没规矩了。胡老爷，你不要理她！等我收拾桌子泡茶来你吃。”
en: A’zhu was angry. He had clearly been wanting to leave for some time, yet he had to make that clever remark. Turning outwards, she deliberately drew out her words as she called to the boat hand. “A’si! Put out the gangplank! Our guest is leaving!” “It's still early!” her mother immediately answered. “Stay a little longer, Mr Hu.” “Don't keep him! It's getting dark, it's going to rain, the road will be bad. If he slips, he'll blame you!” Plainly she was speaking in a temper, yet her clear, birdlike voice made it sound only pleasing and amusing. Hu could not bring himself to insist on leaving. “I'm not going,” he said with a smile. “A’zhu is driving me away.” “There she goes, forgetting her manners again. Pay no attention to her, Mr Hu. I'll clear the table and make you some tea.”

zh: 等收拾了桌子，重新泡上一碗上品龙井新茶来，天气果然变了，船篷上滴滴答答响起了雨声。“黄梅天，说睛就晴，一下工夫，天又好了。”阿珠的娘说这话的用意，胡雪岩当然知道，是唯恐他要走，或者虽不走而记挂着天黑雨滑，道路泥泞，不能安心坐下来。他向来不肯让人有这种悬揣不安的感觉，心想既来之则安之，真的要走，哪怕三更半夜，天上下冰雹，总也得想出办法来脱身，那就不如放大方些。于是他说，“随它下好了，反正不好走就不好走，你们船上我又不是没有住过。”这一说，她们母女俩脸上的神色，立刻就都不同的。“是啊！”阿珠的娘的，“明天一早走也一样。”“不过我今天晚上实在有件要紧事。也罢，”他慨然说道，“我写封信，请你们那位伙计，替我送一送。”“好的！”阿珠的娘要吩咐她女儿去取笔砚，谁知阿珠的心里来得快，早就在动手了。
en: By the time the table had been cleared and a fresh bowl of the finest new Longjing tea prepared, the weather had indeed changed. Rain began pattering on the boat's awning. “In the plum-rain season it clears as suddenly as it clouds over. The weather will be fine again in a moment.” Hu understood why A’zhu's mother said this. She feared he would leave—or, even if he stayed, that he would be too worried about darkness, rain, and muddy roads to sit at ease. He never liked to leave others in such anxious uncertainty. Since he was here, he might as well settle down. If he truly wished to leave, he would have to find a way, even at midnight in a hailstorm. Better, then, to be generous about it. “Let it rain,” he said. “If the journey's difficult, it's difficult. It wouldn't be the first time I've slept on your boat.” Mother and daughter immediately brightened. “Exactly!” her mother said. “You can just as well leave first thing tomorrow.” “But I really do have important business this evening. Never mind,” he said expansively. “I'll write a note and ask your boat hand to deliver it.” “Certainly!” Her mother was about to tell A’zhu to fetch the writing things, but the quick-thinking girl was already doing so.

zh: 打开柜子取出一个红木盘，文房四宝，一应俱全。原是为客人预备的，只是久已不用，砚墨尘封，阿珠抹一抹干净，随手伸出春葱样的一只指头，在自己的茶碗里蘸了几滴水珠，注入砚中，替他磨墨。她磨墨，他在腹中打草稿，此是胡雪岩的一短，几句话想了好半天，把张信纸在桌上抹了又抹，取支笔在砚台中舐了又舐，才算想停当。信是写给刘庆生的，请他去通知自己家里，只说：今夜因为王有龄有要紧公事，要彻夜会商，不能回家。其实这么两句话，叫船伙计阿四到自己家去送个口信，反倒简便，只是胡雪岩怕阿四去了，会泄漏自己的行踪，所以特意转这样一道手。办了这件事，胡雪岩就轻松了，但阿珠看在眼里，却又不免猜疑，胡雪岩怕是个怕老婆的人？转念又想，这正是胡雪岩的好处，换了那些浪荡子弟，自己在外面花天酒地，把太太丢在家，独守空房，哪怕提心吊胆，一夜坐等，也不会放在他心上。
en: She opened a cupboard and took out a rosewood tray containing a complete set of writing materials: brush, inkstick, paper, and inkstone. They had been provided for passengers but had not been used for so long that the inkstone and inkstick were dusty. A’zhu wiped them clean, dipped a slender finger into her tea bowl, transferred a few drops to the inkstone, and began grinding ink for him. While she worked, he composed the note in his head. Writing was one of his weaknesses. Even these few sentences took considerable thought. He repeatedly smoothed the paper on the table and worked the brush against the inkstone before he finally settled on the wording. The note was addressed to Liu Qingsheng, asking him to tell Hu's household that urgent official business with Wang Youling required an all-night consultation and that he could not return home. It would have been simpler to send A’si directly to the house with this brief message. But Hu feared the boat hand would reveal his whereabouts, so he deliberately chose this roundabout route. With the matter settled, Hu relaxed. Watching him, A’zhu wondered whether he might be afraid of his wife. Then she reconsidered: this was one of his virtues. A dissolute young man would go out carousing and leave his wife alone at home without caring whether she spent the whole night waiting in fear and anxiety.

zh: “好了！”他喝着茶说，“有事，你就谈吧！”明明有终身大事要谈，说破了，阿珠反倒不愿，“你这个人！”她说，“一定要有事谈，才留你在这里吗？”“就是闲谈，总也要有件事。”胡雪岩问道，“阿珠，你在湖州住过几年？”“那怎么说得出？来来去去，算不清楚了。”“湖州地方你总很熟是不是？”“当然不会陌生。不过也不是顶熟。”阿珠又说，“你问它做什么？”“王大老爷放了湖州府，我总要打听打听那里的情形。”“我倒问你。”阿珠忽然然注意地，“你是不是也要到湖州去做官？”这话让胡雪岩很难回答，想了一会答道：“湖州我是要常去的。不过，至多是半官半商。”
en: “Now, then!” he said over his tea. “If there's anything you want to discuss, go ahead.” There certainly was the question of her future marriage, but his putting it so plainly made A’zhu reluctant. “Really, you!” she said. “Must there be something to discuss before I can ask you to stay?” “Even idle conversation needs a subject. A’zhu, how many years have you lived in Huzhou?” “How could I say? We've come and gone so often that I've lost count.” “But you know the place well?” “I'm certainly no stranger to it, though I don't know it better than anyone. Why do you ask?” “Now that Mr Wang is going to be prefect there, I ought to learn something about it.” “Then let me ask you,” she said, suddenly attentive. “Are you going to Huzhou to become an official too?” Hu found that difficult to answer. After thinking a moment, he said, “I shall go to Huzhou often. But at most I'll be half official, half merchant.”

zh: “怎么叫‘半官半商’？又做官又做生意？”阿珠心中灵光一闪，就象黑夜里在荒野中迷路，忽然一道闪电，恰好让她辨清了方向，不由得精神大振，急急问道：“你要到湖州做啥生意？是不是开钱庄。”“不是开钱庄。”胡雪岩答说：“我想做丝生意。”“这就一定要到湖州去！”阿珠很高光，也很骄傲地说：“我们湖州的丝，天下第一！”“是啊！因为天下第一，所以外国人也要来买。”阿珠说的“天下”，是照多少年来传统的定义，四海之内，就是天下。胡雪岩到过上海，晓得了西洋的情形，才知道天外有天，人外有人，所以他口中的天下，跟阿珠所想的不同。
en: “What does ‘half official, half merchant’ mean? Holding office and doing business?” A sudden inspiration flashed through A’zhu's mind, like lightning revealing the right direction to someone lost in the wilderness at night. Her spirits rose at once. “What business will you do in Huzhou?” she asked eagerly. “Open a bank?” “Not a bank,” Hu replied. “I'm thinking of going into silk.” “Then you certainly must go to Huzhou!” she said with delighted pride. “Our Huzhou silk is the finest in the world!” “Yes. That's why foreigners come to buy it too.” By “the world,” A’zhu meant what people had traditionally meant for generations: the realm within the four seas. Hu had visited Shanghai and learnt something of the West. He now knew that there were skies beyond his own sky and people beyond his familiar world. The world he meant was therefore different from the one she imagined.

zh: “原来你买了丝要去‘销洋庄’！”阿珠说道，“销洋庄的丝，一直都是广帮客人的生意。”“别人好做，我也好做。”胡雪岩笑道：“阿珠，看样子，你倒不外行。”“当然罗，”她扬着脸，挺直了身子，显得很神气地，“你想想，我是什么地方人？”“那好！你把你们湖州出丝的情形倒讲给我听听看。”阿珠知道，这不是闲谈，胡雪岩既然要做这行生意，当然要先打听得越清楚越好，她怕自己说得不够明白，甚至说错，因而把她娘也去搬请了来，一起来细谈。
en: “So you mean to buy silk for the export houses!” A’zhu said. “That's always been the business of the Cantonese merchants.” “If others can do it, so can I.” Hu smiled. “You don't seem altogether ignorant of the trade, A’zhu.” “Of course not!” She lifted her face and straightened proudly. “Think where I come from!” “Good! Then tell me how silk is produced in Huzhou.” She knew this was no longer idle talk. If Hu intended to enter the trade, naturally he wanted as much precise information as possible. Afraid she might explain badly or even get something wrong, she fetched her mother to discuss it with them in detail.

adaptation.reason: 将已知未成年人物被突出描写的身体部位中性化，保留自豪神态、挺直身子的动作与原有对话。

zh: “这个，”阿珠的娘说，“我们无锡乡下也养蚕的，不过出的多是‘肥丝’，不比湖州多是‘细丝’……”“怎么叫‘肥丝’？”胡雪岩打断她的话问。“丝分三种，上等茧子缫成细丝，上、中茧缫成肥丝，下等茧子缫成的就是粗丝。粗丝不能上织机，织绸一定得用肥丝和细丝，细丝为经，肥丝为纬。”这一说，胡雪岩立即就懂了细丝质地高于肥丝的道理，因为杭州的“织造衙门”，下城一带，“机坊”林立，他也听人说过，一定要坚韧光亮的好丝，才能做“经”丝。
en: “Well,” her mother began, “we raise silkworms in the countryside round Wuxi too. But most of our output is what we call full silk, whereas Huzhou produces chiefly fine silk...” “What is full silk?” Hu interrupted. “There are three grades. The best cocoons are reeled into fine silk. Good and medium cocoons produce full silk. Poor cocoons yield coarse silk. Coarse silk can't be put on the loom. Woven silk requires the fine and full grades: fine silk for the warp, full silk for the weft.” Hu immediately understood why the fine grade was superior. Near Hangzhou's Imperial Silk Weaving Office, in the lower part of the city, there were weaving workshops everywhere. He had heard that only good silk, strong and lustrous, could serve as warp thread.

zh: “在湖州，女孩子十一二岁就懂养蚕，养蚕实在辛苦，三、四月里称为‘蚕月’，真正是六亲不认，门口贴张红纸就是‘挡箭牌’，哪怕邻舍都不往来。““听说还有许多禁忌，是不是？”“禁忌来得个多。”阿珠的娘说，“夫妇不能同房，也不能说什么风言风语，因为‘蚕宝宝’最要干净。”接下来，她细谈了养蚕的过程，由初生到成茧，经过“三眠”，大概要二十八天到四十天的工夫，喂蚕有定时，深更半夜，都得起身饲食，耽误不得一刻。育蚕又最重温度，门窗紧闭，密不通风，如果天气骤变，觉得冷了，必须生火，常有些养蚕人家，不知不觉间倦极而眠，以致失火成灾。育蚕当然要桑叶，空有桑树，固然无用，蚕多桑少，也是麻烦，有时不得不把辛苦养成一半的蚕弃置。这是养蚕人家最痛苦的事。
en: “In Huzhou, girls know how to raise silkworms by eleven or twelve. It's hard work. The third and fourth months are called the silkworm months. People really do shut out even their closest relations. A sheet of red paper on the door serves as a shield against visitors. They don't even see their neighbours.” “I've heard there are many taboos too. Is that right?” “A great many,” A’zhu's mother replied. “Husband and wife mustn't sleep together, nor must anyone use improper language. The silkworm babies demand complete purity.” She went on to describe the process in detail. From hatching to cocooning, the worms passed through three periods of dormancy, taking roughly twenty-eight to forty days. They had to be fed at set times; even in the middle of the night, someone must rise to feed them without a moment's delay. Temperature was especially important. Doors and windows were kept tightly shut against draughts. If the weather changed suddenly and the room grew cold, a fire had to be lit. Often exhausted members of silkworm-raising households fell asleep unawares, allowing fires to break out and cause disaster. Of course, the worms needed mulberry leaves. Mulberry trees alone were useless, but too many worms and too few trees also caused difficulties. Sometimes people had to discard worms already halfway through their painstaking upbringing. Nothing was more painful to a silkworm-raising household.

zh: 这一谈，把胡雪岩记忆中的关于蚕丝的知识勾了出来，便即问道，“最好的丝，是不是叫‘缉里丝’？”“大家都这么说。”阿珠的娘答道，“那地方离南浔七里路。”“原来是‘七里丝’，不是‘缉里丝’。”胡雪岩欣然领悟，“真是凡事要请教内行。”“七”与“缉”字异而音同，所以阿珠听得莫名其妙，在旁边笑他：“什么‘七里丝’不是‘七里丝’？姓胡的，不姓胡，这叫什么怪话？”
en: Her account brought back what Hu already knew of silk. “Isn't the very best called Jili silk?” he asked. “That's what everyone says,” A’zhu's mother answered. “The place is seven li from Nanxun.” “So it's Qili—‘seven li’—silk, rather than Jili!” Hu exclaimed, pleased with his discovery. “You really must consult those who know the trade.” The characters for “seven” and the first syllable of Jili were different, but sounded alike in their speech. A’zhu was therefore puzzled and laughed at him. “What do you mean, ‘Qili silk, not Qili silk’? A man named Hu isn't named Hu? What sort of nonsense is that?”

zh: 胡雪岩笑笑不答，这时没有心里来跟她斗嘴开玩笑，他脑中有七八个念头在转，自己静一静，略略理出了一个头绪，才重拾中断的话题。“养蚕我是明白了。怎么样缫丝，丝做出来，怎么卖出去，我还不大懂。”于是阿珠的娘，把土法缫丝的方法讲给他听，用一口大锅，烧滚了水，倒一升茧下去，用根木棍子搅着，锅上架两部小丝车，下面装一根竹管，等把丝头搅了出来，通过竹管，绕小车一匝，再引入地上的大丝车。抽尽了丝，蚕蛹自然出现，如果丝断了再搅，搅出丝头来，抽光了为止。“缫丝也辛苦。”阿珠的娘的说，“茧子不赶紧缫出丝来，里头的蛹咬破了头，茧子就没有用了。所以缫丝一定是一家大小动手，没日没夜赶完为止。胡老爷你想想看，站在滚烫的小锅旁边，不停手的搅，不停手的抽丝，加以蚕蛹烫死了的那股气味，真正是受罪。倘或遇着茧子潮软，抽丝不容易，那就越发苦了。还有搅了半天，抽不出头的，那叫‘水茧’，只好捞出来丢掉，白费心血。”
en: Hu smiled without answering. He had no inclination to exchange jokes just then. Seven or eight ideas were turning in his mind. He quietened himself, began to put them in order, and returned to the interrupted subject. “I understand how the worms are raised now. What I still don't quite understand is how the silk is reeled and then sold.” A’zhu's mother explained the traditional method. Water was boiled in a large pot, a sheng measure of cocoons tipped in, and the contents stirred with a wooden stick. Two small reels stood above the pot, with a bamboo tube beneath. Once stirring had drawn out the filament ends, these were passed through the tube, taken once round a small reel, and led to the large reel on the ground. As the silk was drawn off, the pupae appeared. If a thread broke, one stirred again to find its end, continuing until all the silk had been reeled. “Reeling is hard work too,” she said. “Unless the cocoons are reeled quickly, the creatures inside break through them and make them useless. So the whole family, young and old, has to work day and night until it's finished. Imagine standing beside a pot of boiling water, stirring and drawing silk without stopping, with that smell from the scalded pupae. It's real suffering. If the cocoons are damp and soft and won't reel easily, it's worse still. Some won't yield an end however long you stir. They're called water cocoons. You can only fish them out and throw them away—all that work wasted.”

zh: “苦虽苦，总也有开心的时候。”“当然罗，一直是苦的事情，天下没有人去做的。到缫成丝，‘丝客人’一到镇上，那就是开心的时候到了，丝价年年在涨，新丝卖来的钱，着实可以派点用场。”这触及到胡雪岩最需要了解的地方了。“丝客人”这个名称，他是懂的，带了大批现银到产地买丝的，称为“丝客人”，开丝行代为搜购新丝，从中取利的称为“丝主人”。每到三、四月间，钱庄放款给丝客人是一项主要的业务。他在想，与其政款给丝客人去买丝，赚取拆息，何不自己做丝客人？“我也想做做丝客人。不知道其中有什么诀窍？”“这我就不晓得了。”阿珠的娘说，“照我想，第一总要懂得丝好坏。第二，要晓得丝的行情，丝价每年有上落，不过收新丝总是便宜的。“
en: “Hard as it is, there must be happy times too.” “Of course. Nobody in the world would do something that was nothing but misery. Once the silk is reeled and the travelling silk buyers reach town, the happy time begins. Silk prices rise every year. The money from the new silk really does come in useful.” Here was what Hu most needed to understand. He knew the term “travelling silk buyer”: a merchant who brought large quantities of ready silver to purchase silk where it was produced. Those who operated local firms, gathering new silk for the buyers and making a profit in the process, were known as “silk hosts.” Every third and fourth month, lending to the travelling buyers was one of the banks' chief lines of business. Why, Hu thought, should he lend them money to buy silk and collect interest, instead of becoming a buyer himself? “I'd like to try being a silk buyer too. Are there any special tricks to it?” “That I couldn't tell you,” A’zhu's mother replied. “I suppose the first thing is to recognise good silk. The second is to know the market. Prices go up and down each year, but buying the new season's silk is always cheaper.”

zh: “丝价的上落，是怎么来的呢？出得少，价钱就高，或者收的人多，价钱也会高。是不是这样子？”“我想做生意总是这样。不过，”阿珠的娘又说，“丝价高低，我听人说，一大半是‘做’出来的，都有几个大户手里。”听得这话，胡雪岩精神一振，知道丝价高低，决于大户的操纵，这个把戏他最在行。阿珠的娘这时越谈越起劲了，而且所谈的也正是胡雪岩想知道的，茧与丝的买卖。“如果人手不够，或者别样缘故，卖茧子的也有。”她说，“收茧子的有茧行，要官府里领了‘牙帖’才好开。同行有‘茧业公所’，新茧上市，同行公议，哪一天开称，哪一天为止。价钱也是议好的，不准自己拾价。不过乡下人卖茧子常要吃亏，除非万不得已，都是卖丝。”
en: “What makes the price rise and fall? If less silk is produced, the price goes up; or if more people want to buy it, that raises the price too. Is that how it works?” “I suppose all business works that way. But,” she added, “I've heard that silk prices are mostly made by people. They're in the hands of a few big firms.” Hu's spirits rose. So prices depended on manipulation by the large operators. That was a game he understood exceptionally well. A’zhu's mother was becoming increasingly animated, and she was discussing exactly what he wanted to know: the buying and selling of cocoons and silk. “Some families sell their cocoons because they don't have enough hands, or for some other reason,” she said. “Cocoon firms buy them. To open one, you have to obtain a broker's licence from the authorities. The trade has its Cocoon Guild. When the new cocoons reach the market, the members agree on the day buying begins and the day it ends. They agree on the prices too; nobody may raise them independently. But country people often lose out by selling cocoons. Unless they have no other choice, they sell silk.”

zh: “为什么要吃亏？”“这一点你都不懂？”阿珠插嘴，“茧行杀你的价，你只好卖，不卖摆在那里，里头的蛹咬破了头，一文不值！”“对，对！我也搅糊涂了。”胡雪岩又问：“那么茧子行买了茧子，怎么出手呢？”“ 这有两种，一种是卖给缫丝厂，一种是自己缫了丝卖。”“喔，我懂了。你倒再说说丝行看，也要向部里领牙帖，也有同业公所？”
en: “Why do they lose out?” “Don't you understand even that?” A’zhu interrupted. “If the cocoon firm beats down your price, you have to sell. Leave them unsold, and the creatures inside break through. Then they're not worth a single copper!” “Yes, yes! I wasn't thinking.” Hu asked another question. “Once the cocoon firm has bought them, how does it sell them on?” “There are two ways. It can sell them to a reeling establishment, or reel the silk itself and sell that.” “Ah, I see. Now tell me about the silk firms. Do they also need a broker's licence from the ministry? And do they have a guild?”

zh: “当然罗。丝行的花样比茧行多得多，各做各的生意，大的才叫丝行，小的叫‘用户’，当地买，当地用，中间转手批发的叫‘划庄’。还有‘广行’、‘洋庄’，专门做洋鬼子的生意，那是越发要大本钱了，上万‘两’的丝摆在手里，等价钱好了卖给洋鬼子，你想想看，要压多少本钱？洋鬼子也坏得很，你抬他的价，他不说你贵，表面跟你笑嘻嘻，暗夜下另外去寻路子，自有吃本太重，急于想脱手求现的，肯杀价卖给他。你还在那里老等，人家已经塌进便宜货，装上轮船运到西洋去了……”“慢，慢来！”胡雪岩大声打断，“等我想一想。”
en: “Of course. There are far more varieties of silk firm than cocoon firm, each with its own business. Only the larger ones are properly called silk firms. The smaller ones are ‘users,’ buying locally for local use. Those that buy and resell wholesale are called ‘transfer houses.’ Then there are Cantonese houses and export houses, which deal exclusively with the foreign devils. Those require even more capital. They may hold tens of thousands of liang in silk, waiting for a good price before selling it to the foreigners. Think how much capital that ties up! And the foreign devils are very cunning. If you ask a higher price, they don't tell you you're expensive. They smile pleasantly while secretly looking elsewhere. There's always someone with too much money tied up, desperate to sell for cash and willing to take a lower price. You go on waiting while they've already bought cheap stock, put it on a steamship, and sent it to the West...” “Wait, wait!” Hu interrupted loudly. “Let me think.”

zh: 她们母女俩都不晓得他要想什么？只见他皱紧眉头，偏着头，双眼望着空中，是极用心的样子，他在想嫌洋鬼子的钱！做生意就怕心不齐，跟洋鬼子做生意，也要象茧行收茧一样，就是这个价钱，愿意就愿意，不愿意就拉倒。那一来洋鬼子非服帖不可。不过人心不同，各如其面，但也难怪，本钱不足，周转不灵，只好脱货求现，除非……他豁然贯通了！除非能把所有的“洋庄”都抓在手里。当然，天下的饭，一个人是吃不完的，只有联络同行，要他们跟着自己走。
en: Neither mother nor daughter knew what he wanted to think about. They saw him frown, tilt his head, and stare into space in deep concentration. He was thinking how to make money out of the foreigners. The great danger in business was lack of unity. Dealing with foreigners should be like the cocoon firms' buying arrangements: this was the price; take it or leave it. Then the foreigners would have to submit. But people's minds differed as much as their faces. Nor could one really blame them. With insufficient capital and no money circulating, they had no choice but to sell for cash, unless... Suddenly he saw it! Unless he could bring all the export houses under his influence. Naturally, no one person could swallow every opportunity in the world. He must bring his fellow merchants together and persuade them to follow his lead.

zh: 这也不难！他在想，洋庄丝价卖得好，哪个不乐意？至于想脱货求现的，有两个办法，第一，你要卖给洋鬼子，不如卖给我。第二，你如果不肯卖给我，也不要卖给洋鬼子，要用多少款子，拿货色来抵押，包他将来能嫌得比现在多。这样，此人如果还一定要卖货色给洋鬼子，那必定是暗底下受人家的好处，有意自贬身价，成了吃里扒外的半吊子，可以鼓动同行，跟他断绝往来，看他还狠到哪里去？“对啊，对啊！”他想到得意之处，自己拍着手掌笑，仿佛痰迷心窍似地，把阿珠逗得笑弯了腰。阿珠的娘，到底不同，有几分猜到，便即笑着问道：“胡老爷是想做丝生意？”“我要做‘丝客人’。”“果不其然！”阿珠的娘得意的笑了，“胡老爷要做丝生意。”阿珠当然更是喜心翻倒，不仅是为了这一来常有跟胡雪岩聚会的机会，而且也因为自己的心愿，居然很快地就达成，所以有着近乎意外的那种惊喜。
en: That would not be difficult either. Who would object to higher prices for export silk? For those who needed to sell for cash, there were two solutions. First: instead of selling to the foreigners, sell to him. Second: if they would not sell to him, they should still refrain from selling to the foreigners. Whatever funds they needed, they could borrow against their goods; he would guarantee them a better profit later than they could make now. If a man still insisted on selling to the foreigners, he must be receiving secret benefits from them, deliberately lowering his own price and betraying his fellows for outsiders. Hu could rally the trade to cut off all dealings with him. Then how far could his defiance go? “That's it! That's it!” Carried away by his cleverness, he clapped and laughed to himself as though possessed, making A’zhu double up with laughter. Her mother was different: she partly guessed his thoughts. “Are you planning to enter the silk trade, Mr Hu?” she asked with a smile. “I mean to become a travelling silk buyer.” “Just as I thought!” she said triumphantly. “Mr Hu means to trade in silk.” A’zhu, of course, was even more delighted. It was not only that she would have frequent opportunities to see him. Her own wish seemed to have come true so quickly that she felt the joyful surprise of an unexpected gift.

zh: “不过，干娘……”胡雪岩这样叫阿珠的娘。那是杭州人习用的一种称呼，还是南宋的遗风，义母叫干娘，姑母也叫干娘，凡是对年纪比自己大的妇人而自愿执后辈之礼的，都可以这样称呼。因此这一叫，叫得阿珠的娘，受宠若惊。“不敢当，不敢当！”她连连逊谢，近乎惶恐的，“胡老爷千万不要这样叫！”她在谦虚，阿珠却在旁边急坏了！这一声“干娘”，在她听来就如胡雪岩跟她开那个玩笑，说要叫娘为‘丈母娘“是差不多的意思，所以表面没有什么，心一直在跳。她想：人家要来亲近，你偏偏不受，这算什么意思呢？因此，胡雪岩还没有开口，她先发了话：“人家抬举你，你不要不识抬举！”知女莫若母，胡雪岩的“干娘”，立即有所意会，她自己也觉得大可不必如此坚辞不受。不过也不便把话拉回来，最好含含糊糊过去，等你再叫时不作声，那一下“干娘”就做定了。于是她笑着骂阿珠：“你看你，倒过来教训起我来了！”
en: “But, Auntie...” Hu addressed A’zhu's mother as ganniang, a form familiar in Hangzhou and inherited from the Southern Song. It could mean an adoptive mother or a paternal aunt, and could be used for any older woman towards whom the speaker voluntarily assumed the respectful position of a younger relation. A’zhu's mother was overwhelmed by the honour. “Oh, I couldn't accept that!” she protested repeatedly, almost alarmed. “You mustn't call me that, Mr Hu!” While her mother demurred, A’zhu grew anxious. To her, “Auntie” meant almost the same thing as his earlier joke about calling Mother his mother-in-law. She appeared calm, but her heart kept racing. He was trying to draw closer, and Mother insisted on refusing. What sense did that make? Before Hu could answer, she spoke. “He's honouring you. Don't be so ungracious!” No one understands a daughter better than her mother. Hu's new “Auntie” immediately grasped what A’zhu meant and realised that there was no need to refuse so firmly. Yet she could hardly take back her words. Best to let the matter pass vaguely, then make no objection when he used the name again. That would settle her new position. She laughed and scolded A’zhu. “Look at you! Now you're the one lecturing me!”

zh: 她们母女俩的语气眼风，一五一十都看在胡雪岩眼里，此时忙着要谈正经，没有工夫理这回来，“干娘！”他说，“我做‘丝客人’，你做‘丝主人’好不好？”“胡老爷在说笑话了。”做“丝主人”就是开丝行，阿珠的娘说，“我又不开丝行，哪里有丝卖给你？”“不要紧！我来帮你开。”“开什么？”阿珠又插嘴，“开丝行？”“对！”答得非常爽脆。阿珠的娘看看他，又看看女儿，这样子不象说笑话。但如果不是笑话，却更让她困惑，“胡老爷，”她很谨慎地问：“你自己为什么不来开？”“这话问得对了！”胡雪岩连连点头，“为什么我自己不来开呢？第一，我不是湖州人，做生意，老实说，总有点欺生的。第二，王大老爷在湖州府，我来做‘客人’不要紧，来做‘主人’，人家就要说闲话了。明明跟王大老爷无关，说起来某某丝行有知府撑腰，遭人的忌，生意就难做了。”
en: Hu noticed every tone and glance exchanged by mother and daughter, but he was too eager to discuss serious business to attend to their meaning. “Auntie,” he said, “if I become a travelling silk buyer, how would you like to become a silk host?” “You're joking, Mr Hu.” Being a silk host meant operating a local silk firm. “I haven't got a silk firm. Where would I find silk to sell you?” “Never mind. I'll help you open one.” “Open what?” A’zhu broke in again. “A silk firm?” “Yes!” His answer was crisp and confident. Her mother looked from him to her daughter. He did not seem to be joking. But if he was serious, that was even more puzzling. “Mr Hu,” she asked cautiously, “why don't you open one yourself?” “That's exactly the right question!” Hu nodded repeatedly. “Why don't I? First, I'm not from Huzhou, and in business, to be frank, people do take advantage of newcomers. Second, Mr Wang will be prefect there. If I come as a visiting buyer, that's harmless; if I become a local proprietor, people will gossip. Though Mr Wang has nothing to do with it, they'll say such-and-such a firm has the prefect behind it. That breeds resentment and makes business difficult.”

zh: 这一说阿珠的娘才明白。一想到自己会有个现成的“老板娘”做，笑得眼睛眯成两条缝，“原来胡大老爷要我出出面。不过，”她的心又一冷，“我女人家，怎么出面？”“那不要紧，请你们老张来出面领帖，暗底下，是你老板娘一把抓，那不也一样吗？”“啊唷！老板娘！”阿珠甩着辫子大笑，“又是干娘，又是老板娘，以后我要好好巴结你了！”那笑声有些轻狂，以至于把她爹招引了来，探头一望，正好让胡雪岩发觉，随即招着手说：“来，来，老张！正有事要跟你谈。”老张是个老实人，见了胡雪岩相当拘谨，斜欠着身子坐在椅子上，仿佛下属对上司似地，静听吩咐。胡雪岩看这样子，觉得不宜于郑重的态度来谈正经，就叫阿珠说明因由。
en: Now A’zhu's mother understood. At the thought of stepping straight into the role of a business proprietor, she smiled until her eyes narrowed to two slits. “So you want me to represent the firm, Mr Hu. But...” Her spirits suddenly sank. “How can a woman take that public role?” “That's no difficulty. Have Old Zhang apply for the licence in his name. Behind the scenes, you'll run everything as the proprietress. Won't that amount to the same thing?” “Oh my! The proprietress!” A’zhu tossed her braid and laughed. “An auntie and a proprietress! I shall have to make myself very agreeable to you from now on!” Her laughter was rather exuberant and brought her father to see what was happening. As he peered in, Hu noticed him and beckoned. “Come in, Old Zhang! There's something I want to discuss with you.” An honest, simple man, Old Zhang was quite constrained in Hu's presence. He perched sideways on the edge of a chair, listening for instructions like a subordinate before his superior. Seeing this, Hu thought a solemn business discussion would be unsuitable and asked A’zhu to explain.

zh: “胡老爷要挑你做老板！”阿珠用这样一句话开头，口气象是局外人，接着把胡雪岩的意思，仔仔细细他说了一遍。老张也是做梦都没有想到，听了妻子的话，为打听胡雪岩的信址到信和去了一趟，撞出这么一件喜事来，不过，他也多少有些疑惑，觉得事太突兀，未见得如阿珠所说的那么好。因此，他说话就有保留了，“多谢胡老爷，”他慢吞吞地，“事情倒是件好事，我也有一两个丝行里的朋友，只怕我做不好。”“哪个生来就会的？老张，你听我说，做生意第一要齐心，第二要人缘，我想你人缘不坏的，只要听我话，别的我不敢说，无论如何我叫你日子比在船上过得舒服。”胡雪岩接着又说：“一个人总要想想后半世，弄只船飘来飘去，不是个了局！”就这一句话，立刻打动了老张的心，他妻子和女儿当然更觉得动听，“胡老爷这句话，真正实在！”他妻子说，“转眼五十岁的人，吃辛苦也吃不起了，趁现在早早作个打算。我们好歹帮胡老爷把丝行开起来，叶落归根总算也有个一定的地方。”
en: “Mr Hu wants to make you a proprietor!” A’zhu began, in the tone of someone who had no personal interest in the matter. Then she carefully explained his proposal. Old Zhang had never dreamed that obeying his wife's instruction to visit Xinhe and inquire for Hu's address would lead to such good fortune. Yet he had doubts. It was all too sudden and might not be as favourable as A’zhu made it sound. He therefore answered cautiously. “Thank you, Mr Hu,” he said slowly. “It sounds a good opportunity. I do have one or two friends in silk firms. But I'm afraid I might not manage it properly.” “Who is born knowing everything? Listen, Old Zhang. In business, the first thing is to work together; the second is to get on with people. I imagine you're well liked. As long as you follow my advice, I won't promise anything else, but I'll certainly make your life more comfortable than it is on the boat.” He added, “A man must think about the latter half of his life. Drifting about in a boat for ever is no lasting arrangement.” That sentence immediately touched Old Zhang. His wife and daughter naturally found it even more welcome. “That's sound sense, Mr Hu!” his wife said. “He's nearly fifty. He can't go on bearing hard work for ever. Better make plans while there's time. If we can help you establish this firm, we'll at least have a fixed place to return to, like leaves falling back to their roots.”

zh: “不是你们帮我开丝行！”是我帮你们开丝行。“胡雪岩很郑重地，”既然你们有丝行里的朋友，那再好不过。老张，我倒先要问你，开丝行要多少本钱？““那要看丝行大小。一个门面，一副生财，两三百两银子现款，替客户代代手，也是丝行，自己买了丝囤在那里，专等客户上门，也是丝行。”“照这样说，有一千两银子可以开了？”“一千两银子本钱，也不算小同行了。”“那好！”胡雪岩把视线扫过他们夫妻父女，最后落在老张脸上，“我不说送，我借一千两银子给你！你开丝行，我托你买丝。一千两银子不要利息，等你赚了钱就还我。你看好不好？”
en: “You aren't helping me open a silk firm. I'm helping you open one,” Hu said firmly. “And if you already have friends in the trade, so much the better. First, Old Zhang, how much capital would it take?” “That depends on the size. A shopfront, some fittings, and two or three hundred taels in ready money would let you act as an intermediary for customers. That's a silk firm. Buying silk yourself, holding it in stock, and waiting for customers to come—that's a silk firm too.” “Then a thousand taels would be enough to begin?” “With a thousand taels, you wouldn't count as one of the smaller firms.” “Good!” Hu looked round at the couple and their daughter, finally fixing his gaze on Old Zhang. “I won't call it a gift. I'll lend you a thousand taels. You open the firm, and I'll commission you to buy silk. There'll be no interest on the thousand. Repay me when you've made a profit. How does that sound?”

zh: “那怎么不好？”老张答道：“不过，胡老爷，做生意有赚有蚀，万一本钱蚀光了怎么办？”“真正是！”他妻子大为不满，“生意还没有做，先说不识头的话。”“不！干娘，”胡雪岩却很欣赏老张的态度，“做生意就是要这个样子。顾前不顾后，一门心里想赚，那种生意做不好的。这样，老张，我劝你这条船不要卖，租了给人家，万一丝行‘倒灶’，你还可以靠船租过日子。“老张怔怔地不作声，他有些心不在焉，奇怪“胡老爷”怎么一下子叫她妻子为“干娘”？
en: “How could it be anything but good?” Old Zhang answered. “But, Mr Hu, business can make losses as well as profits. What if I lose the whole capital?” “Really!” His wife was indignant. “You haven't even begun, and already you're saying unlucky things.” “No, Auntie.” Hu approved of Old Zhang's attitude. “That's exactly how one ought to approach business. You won't succeed if you look only ahead, neglect what lies behind, and think of nothing but profit. Here is my advice, Old Zhang: don't sell this boat. Hire it out. If the silk firm fails, you can still live on the rent.” Old Zhang stared without speaking. His attention had wandered. Why had Mr Hu suddenly begun calling his wife “Auntie”?

zh: “爹！”阿珠推着他说：“人家在跟你说话？你在想啥心事？”“喔，喔！”老张定定神，才把胡雪岩的话记起来，“胡老爷，”他说：“今年总来不及了！”“怎么呢？”“开丝行要领牙帖，听说要京里发下来，一来一往，最快也要三个月工夫，那时候收丝的辰光早过了。”“收丝也有季节的吗？”“自然罗！”阿珠的娘笑了，“胡老爷，你连这点都不明白？”“隔行如隔山。我从来没有经手过这行生意。不过。”胡雪岩说，“我倒想起来了，钱庄放款给做丝生意的，总在四、五月里。”“是啊，新丝四、五月里上市，都想早早脱手，第一，乡下五荒六月，青黄不接的当口，都等铜钿用。第二，雪白的丝，摆在家里黄了，价钱就要打折扣，也有的想摆一摆，等价钱好了再卖，也不过多等个把月。丝行生意多是一年做一季。“
en: “Father!” A’zhu nudged him. “He's talking to you! What are you thinking about?” “Oh, yes!” Old Zhang collected himself and recalled what Hu had said. “Mr Hu, surely it's too late for this year.” “Why?” “A silk firm needs a broker's licence. I hear it has to come from the capital. Sending the application and getting it back takes at least three months. By then the silk-buying season will be long past.” “Does buying silk have a season too?” “Naturally!” A’zhu's mother laughed. “You don't even know that, Mr Hu?” “Different trades are worlds apart. I've never handled this business. Though,” he added, “now I remember: bank loans to silk merchants are always made in the fourth and fifth months.” “Exactly. The new silk comes on the market then, and everyone wants to sell quickly. First, the lean fifth and sixth months fall between harvests, and people in the countryside are waiting for money. Second, if snow-white silk lies at home until it yellows, its price falls. Some people hold on for a better price, but even they wait only another month or so. Most silk firms do their year's business in a single season.”

zh: 胡雪岩听得这话踌躇了，因为他有一套算盘，王有龄一到湖州，公款解省，当然由他阜康代理“府库”来收支，他的打算是，在湖州收到的现银，就地买丝，运到杭州脱手变现，解交“藩库”，这是无本钱的生意，变戏法不可让外人窥见底蕴，所以他愿意帮老张开丝行。现在听说老张的丝行一时开不成功，买丝运杭州的算盘就打不通了。
en: This made Hu hesitate, for he had a plan of his own. Once Wang arrived in Huzhou, Fukang would naturally handle the prefectural treasury's receipts and payments, including public funds to be remitted to the provincial capital. Hu intended to use the silver received in Huzhou to buy silk there, ship it to Hangzhou, sell it for cash, and pay the money into the provincial treasury. It was business requiring no capital of his own. Outsiders must not see how this conjuring trick worked; that was why he was willing to help Old Zhang open a silk firm. Now, if the firm could not be established immediately, his plan to buy silk and ship it to Hangzhou would fail.

zh: “有这样一个办法，”他问老张：“我们跟人家顶一张，或者租一张牙帖来做。你看行不行？”“这个办法，听倒也听人说过。就不知道要花多少钱？就不定顶一年就要三五面两银子！”“三五百两就三五百两。”胡雪岩说，“小钱不去，大钱不来！老张，你明天就到湖州去办这件事！”想到就做，何至于如此性急？而且一切都还茫无头绪，到了湖州又如何着手？所以老张和他妻儿，都不知如何作答。“胡老爷，”还是阿珠的娘有主意，“我看这样，王大老爷上任，你索性送了去，一船摇到湖州就地办事，你在那里，凡事可以作主，事情就妥当了。”“妥当是妥当，却有两层难处，第一，大家都知道王大老爷跟我，与众不同，我要避嫌，不便送他上任。第二，我有家钱庄，马上要开出来，实在分不开身。”“喔，胡老爷还有家钱庄？”“是的。”胡雪岩说，“钱庄是我出面，背后有大股东。”
en: “What about this?” he asked Old Zhang. “We take over someone else's licence, or rent one. Would that work?” “I've heard of it being done. But I don't know what it would cost. Perhaps three or five hundred taels just for a year!” “Then let it be three or five hundred,” Hu said. “You can't make big money without spending a little. Go to Huzhou tomorrow and arrange it!” Why such haste to act the instant an idea occurred? Nothing was clear yet. How were they to begin once they reached Huzhou? Old Zhang, his wife, and his daughter all found themselves at a loss. Again it was A’zhu's mother who produced an idea. “Mr Hu, why don't you accompany Mr Wang when he takes up his post? We could row straight to Huzhou and deal with things there. With you on the spot to decide everything, it would all go smoothly.” “It would, but there are two difficulties. First, everyone knows how close Mr Wang and I are. I must avoid appearances that might excite suspicion, so I shouldn't accompany him to his appointment. Second, I have a bank about to open. I really can't get away.” “Oh, you have a bank as well?” “Yes,” Hu said. “I represent it publicly. There are major shareholders behind me.”

zh: 这一来，阿珠的娘，越发把胡雪岩看得不同了，她看了他丈夫一眼，转脸问胡雪岩：“那么送到临平……”“那还是照旧。”胡雪岩抢着说，“明天我打一张一千两的银票，请老张带到湖州去，一面弄牙帖，一面看房子，先把门面摆开来。我总在月半左右到湖州来收丝，我想，这船上，老张不在也不要紧吧？”“那要什么紧？”阿珠的娘说，“人手不够，临时雇个短工好了。”谈到这里，便有“不由分说”之势了，老张摇了几十年的船，一下子弃舟登陆，要拿着上千两银子，单枪匹马回湖州开丝行，自有些胆怯，但禁不住他妻儿和胡雪岩的鼓励推动，终于也有了信心，打算着一到湖州；先寻几个丝行朋友商量。好在自己在江湖上走了几十年，纵非人情险，一望而知，人品好歹总识得的，只要这一层上把握得住，就不会吃亏。
en: A’zhu's mother regarded him with still greater respect. She glanced at her husband, then turned back to Hu. “Then the journey to Linping...” “That stands as arranged,” he quickly assured her. “Tomorrow I'll have a banknote made out for a thousand taels, and Old Zhang can take it to Huzhou. He can find a licence and look for premises at the same time, getting the shop set up first. I should come to buy silk around the middle of the month. I suppose the boat can manage without Old Zhang?” “Of course it can,” she replied. “If we're short of hands, we can hire someone temporarily.” By now there was little room for objections. Old Zhang had spent decades rowing a boat. Suddenly to leave it, go ashore, and set out alone for Huzhou with a thousand taels to open a silk firm naturally frightened him. But under the encouragement and urging of Hu, his wife, and his daughter, he at last gained confidence. On arriving, he would first consult a few friends in the trade. After all, he had spent decades travelling the waterways. Even if he could not recognise every danger at a glance, he could judge whether a person's character was good or bad. As long as he held firm to that judgement, he should not be taken advantage of.

zh: 就这样兴高采烈地谈到深夜，阿珠的娘又去弄了消夜来，让胡雪岩吃过。阿珠亲手替他铺好了床，道声“安置”，各自归寝。她心里有好些话要跟他说，但总觉得半夜三更，孤男寡女在一起，是件“大逆不道”的事，所以万般无奈地回到了她自己的铺上。这一夜船上五个人，除了伙计阿四，其作的都有心事在想，所想的也都是开丝行的事，而且也都把阿珠连在一起想，只是各人的想法不同。
en: They talked in high spirits until late at night. A’zhu's mother prepared a late supper for Hu, and after he had eaten, A’zhu made up his bed herself. They wished one another a good night's rest and went to their separate berths. She had much she wanted to say to him, but being alone with a man in the middle of the night seemed to her a shocking impropriety. Reluctantly, she returned to her own bed. Of the five people aboard that night, only A’si had nothing on his mind. The other four were all thinking about the silk firm, and all connected it in their thoughts with A’zhu. Yet each saw it differently.

zh: 最高兴的是阿珠的娘，一下子消除了她心里的两个“疙瘩”，第一个疙瘩是老张快五十岁了，《天雨花》、《再生缘》那些唱本儿上说起来，做官的“年将半百”，便要“告老还乡”，买田买地做“老员外”享清福，而他还在摇船！现在总算叶落归根，可以有个养老送死的“家”了。第二个疙瘩是为了阿珠。把她嫁给胡雪岩，千肯万肯，就怕“做小”受气，虽说胡太太看样子贤慧，但“老爷”到底只有一个，这面恩恩爱爱，那面就凄凄凉凉，日久天长，一定会有气淘。现在把阿珠放在湖州，又不受“大的”气，自己又照顾得到，哪还有比这再好的安排？她一想到此，心满意足。
en: Her mother was the happiest. Two knots of worry had been undone at once. First, Old Zhang was nearly fifty. In such ballad books as Flowers Raining from Heaven and Destined to Meet Again, an official “approaching half a century” would “retire to his native place,” buy fields and land, and enjoy a comfortable old age as a country gentleman. Yet her husband was still rowing a boat! Now at last they could return to their roots and have a home in which to grow old and die. Her second worry concerned A’zhu. She was entirely willing for her daughter to marry Hu, but feared that as a concubine she would suffer. Mrs Hu seemed kind, yet there was only one husband. When he lavished affection on one woman, the other would be left lonely. Over time, resentment was inevitable. If A’zhu stayed in Huzhou, however, she would be free of the senior wife's temper, and her mother would be there to look after her. Could any arrangement be better? The thought left her perfectly content.

zh: 阿珠是比她娘想得更加美。她觉得嫁到胡家，淘气还在其次，“做小”这两个字，总是委屈，难得他情深意重，想出一条“两头大”的路子来！眼前虽未明言，照他的体贴，一定是这么个打算，他现在是先要抬举她爹的身分，做了老板，才好做他的丈人。将来明媒正娶，自己一样凤冠霞帔，坐了花轿来“拜堂”，人家叫起来是“胡太太”，谁也不晓得自己只是“湖州的胡太太”！
en: A’zhu imagined an even happier prospect. If she entered the Hu household, domestic quarrels would be the lesser concern. The very word “concubine” meant accepting an inferior position. How devoted and thoughtful he was to have found a way of giving each of his two households a wife of equal standing! He had not said so yet, but someone so considerate must have that in mind. First he would raise her father's status, making him a proprietor fit to become his father-in-law. Then she would be married openly and properly, with a matchmaker, a phoenix crown, and a ceremonial cape. She would ride in a bridal chair and perform the wedding bows like any other bride. People would call her “Mrs Hu.” No one would know she was only “the Mrs Hu in Huzhou”!

zh: 她那里一厢情愿，另一面胡雪岩也在自度得计。帮老张开丝行，当然也有安置阿珠的意思在内。他也相信看相算命，不过只相信一半，一半天意，一半人事，而人定可以胜天。脱运交运的当口，走不得桃花运，这话固然不错，却要看桃花运是如何走法？如果把阿珠弄回家去，倘或大小不和，三日两头吵得天翻地覆，自己哪里还有心思来做生意？象现在这样，等于自己在湖州开了个丝行，阿珠和她父母会尽力照应。自己到了湖州，当然住在丝行里，阿珠也不算大，也不算小，是个外室，将来看情形再说，果然丝行做得发达了，阿珠就是胡家有功之人，那时把她接回家去，自己妻子也就不好说什么了。他这个念头，看起来面面俱到，事事可行，真正是一把“职意算盘”。
en: While she indulged these hopes, Hu too congratulated himself on his cleverness. Helping Old Zhang establish the firm was certainly intended, in part, to provide an arrangement for A’zhu. He believed in physiognomy and fortune-telling, though only halfway: half was destiny, half human action, and determined human effort could overcome fate. It was true that one should avoid romantic entanglements when passing from one phase of fortune to another. Yet surely that depended on the form the entanglement took. If he brought A’zhu home and wife and concubine quarrelled every few days, turning the house upside down, how could he concentrate on business? Under the present arrangement, it would be as though he had opened his own silk firm in Huzhou, with A’zhu and her parents doing their utmost to manage it. Naturally he would stay there when he visited. A’zhu would be neither senior wife nor household concubine, but a woman maintained in a separate establishment. They could decide the future as circumstances developed. If the firm prospered, she would have rendered the Hu family a real service. When he brought her home then, his wife would have little ground for objection. His plan seemed to cover every angle and make everything practicable. It was indeed a beautifully calculated piece of wishful thinking.

zh: 但是，他再也想不到，老张的心思却变了。他虽是摇船出身，也不识多少字，倒是个有骨气的人。阿珠愿意嫁胡雪岩，自己肯委屈“做小”，他妻子又极力赞成，既然母女俩一条心，他也不反对。照他的想法，将来阿珠到了胡家，不管是大小住在一起，还是另立门户，总归是在杭州，自己做自己的生意，眼不见为净，旁人也不会说什么闲话。此刻不同了。开丝行，做老板，固然是一步登天，求之下得。但旁人不免要问：“摇船的老张，怎么会一下子做了老板？”这话谈下去就很难听了！总不能逢人去分辩：“阿珠给胡某人做小，完全是感情，阿珠自己喜欢他。开丝行是胡某人自己了为做生意方便，就是没有这桩亲事，他依然要开，依然要叫我出面做现成老板！“这话就算自己能够说，别人也未见得相信。所以他这时打定主意，开丝行与阿珠嫁胡雪岩，这两件事决不可夹杂在一起。
en: What he could never have imagined was that Old Zhang's mind had changed. A boatman with little education he might be, but he had self-respect. A’zhu wished to marry Hu and was willing to accept the lesser position; her mother strongly approved. Since mother and daughter were united, he would not oppose them. He had assumed that whether the two women lived together or in separate households, A’zhu would in any case be in Hangzhou. He could carry on his own business, keeping out of what did not concern him, and no one would gossip. Now it was different. Opening a silk firm and becoming a proprietor was certainly a miraculous rise, more than he could have wished for. But people would inevitably ask, “How did Old Zhang the boatman suddenly become a proprietor?” And what followed would be ugly. He could hardly go about explaining to everyone: “A’zhu is becoming Hu's concubine purely because she loves him. The silk firm is for his own business convenience. Even without the marriage, he'd still open it and still ask me to put my name to it and become the proprietor!” Even if he could say all this, others might not believe him. He therefore resolved that opening the silk firm and A’zhu's marriage to Hu must never be mixed together.

zh: “喂！”躺在铺上的老张，推推他妻子，低声问道：“阿珠的事，你们变过了？”“没有。”“那‘他’怎么叫你‘干娘’？”“这是人家客气，抬举我们。”“抬举是不错。不过‘冷粥冷饭好吃，冷言冷语难听’。”“什么冷言冷语。”他妻子很诧异地问，“哪个在嚼舌头？”“也没有人在嚼舌头。是我心里在想……”“好了，好了！”她不耐烦地打断他的话说，“你不要得福不知！该想想正经，到了湖州，寻哪几个朋友，房子看在什么地方？”老张对他妻子，七分敬爱三分怕，听她这语气，如果自己把心里的想法就出来，当夜就会有一场大吵，因而隐忍未言。
en: “Listen,” Old Zhang said softly, nudging his wife as they lay in their berth. “Have you spoken about A’zhu's future?” “No.” “Then why does he call you ‘Auntie’?” “He's being polite and honouring us.” “It is an honour. But cold rice and cold porridge are easy to swallow; cold, cutting words are not.” “What cutting words?” his wife asked in surprise. “Who's been gossiping?” “No one. It's just something I've been thinking...” “There, that's enough!” she interrupted impatiently. “Don't fail to recognise good fortune when it comes! Think about what matters. Which friends will you look up in Huzhou? Where will you find premises?” Old Zhang's feelings towards his wife were seven parts affection and respect, three parts fear. From her tone, he knew that explaining his thoughts would provoke a serious quarrel that very night. He therefore kept them to himself.
